questions.q: What does the summary say about the lone genius myth?
a: No great work was made without help from others
Geniuses do their best work in isolation
Only trained artists can make masterpieces
Competition matters more than collaboration
questions.why: Lesson 1 says every masterpiece depends on curators, friends and sources of inspiration.

questions.q: Why does the author recommend documenting unfinished work?
a: It invites feedback and builds an audience
It stops others from stealing your ideas
It proves you are always busy
It shortens the creative process
questions.why: Lesson 1 says sharing the process brings useful feedback and an audience.

questions.q: Why does the author prefer a website over social media?
a: A domain you own is a safer long-term home
Websites always rank higher in search
Social media cannot reach new people
Websites cost nothing to run forever
questions.why: Lesson 2 warns platforms fade, while an owned website lasts.

questions.q: What should you collect from visitors, per the summary?
a: Email addresses to share updates
Phone numbers for sales calls
Mailing addresses for gifts
Passwords for a members area
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends collecting emails and posting regularly.

questions.q: How does a consistent theme help your platform?
a: It attracts a niche audience that helps each other
It keeps the audience from growing too fast
It lets you post much less often
It hides your work from competitors
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a clear theme draws like-minded people who refer each other.
